clue.text: Lower quality of fish endlessly caught in river

indicators.note: caught in says the shortened fish is held within the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another on the England-Wales border

indicators.note: endlessly tells us to drop the final letter of the fish's name

parts.note: a bass is a fish

explanation.surface: A complaint that the fish pulled from a river is getting worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' reads as an adjective; with 'quality of' it is the verb. The Dee is a familiar crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase something is to degrade it, reducing its worth or standard.

clue.text: One filling in old record in tax

indicators.note: the second in says the record goes inside the word for tax

parts.note: a duty is a tax, as on imports
EP, an extended-play disc, is an old record format

explanation.surface: Someone substituting on an outdated record within a tax form.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy is a stand-in who acts for someone absent.

clue.text: Bandit pays for drink outside new fund-raising event

indicators.note: outside says the run of words for bandit, pays for and drink is placed around the letter for new

parts.note: a brigand is a bandit
buys means pays for
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: An outlaw stands a round outside a new charity event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts the whole run round N, which lands after BRI. A bring-and-buy sale is a British charity sale where people bring goods to sell and buy others'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classic British charity sale, a common church or school way of raising money.

clue.text: Search turned round college

indicators.note: round says the word for turned goes about the college letter

parts.note: milk that has turned has gone sour

explanation.surface: Someone hunting by turning around a college campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' looks like a reversal signal; it is SOUR, as milk turns.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour an area is to search it thoroughly.

clue.text: Sort of craft featured in Time magazine?

parts.note: Woman is a long-running British women's weekly magazine

explanation.surface: A kind of boat or vessel appears in the pages of Time magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time magazine' reads as the American weekly; it is T and the British weekly Woman. 'featured in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-man craft, such as a bobsleigh or canoe, is one crewed by a pair.

clue.text: Casus belli not found post-war — CIA messes up

definitions.text: Casus belli not found post-war — CIA messes up

parts.words: Casus belli not found post-war — CIA messes up
parts.note: the justification given for the 2003 invasion of Iraq: arms said to exist which were never found after the fighting, an intelligence failure

explanation.surface: A war's pretext evaporated afterwards because the intelligence agency blundered.
explanation.walkthrough: A cryptic definition recalling the Iraq war: the arsenal cited as the reason to invade was not found when it was over.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear, chemical and biological arms were the stated cause for war in Iraq and none turned up afterwards.

clue.text: See 5
End of game — playing is done

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with and rearranged

explanation.surface: The match ends: the play is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges IS DONE. In rugby the referee formerly called 'no side' to end the match.
explanation.definitionFit: No side is the traditional rugby term for the final whistle.

clue.text: European Community study cake

parts.note: a study or den is a lair, a private retreat

explanation.surface: A European body examining a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' looks like a verb; it is a room, a den or LAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a long choux pastry filled with cream and iced with chocolate.

clue.text: Thalia perhaps'd make one so

parts.note: Thalia is one of the nine Muses, so she is an example of a muse
'd is the contracted form of would or had, the letter D

explanation.surface: The Muse of comedy would put one in a good humour.
explanation.walkthrough: Thalia is the Muse of comedy, so her influence would leave one entertained; 'perhaps' marks her as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic Muse would leave one entertained and smiling.

clue.text: Formidable opponent, first of grade in rank

indicators.note: in says that letter goes within the word for rank

parts.note: a tier is a rank or level

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word grade

explanation.surface: A tough adversary, the best in their grade, rises through the ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a fierce competitor a tiger likens them to the big cat's ferocity.

clue.text: Vanished duke appearing in Scottish seat-what could be bad about that

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the rest
could be signals that the letters of bad might be rearranged
appearing in says the duke's letter is placed inside the Scottish place name

parts.note: Scone, near Perth, is where Scottish kings were crowned on the Stone of Scone

explanation.surface: A duke turned up at a Scottish seat and disappeared, which looks bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing in' makes SCONDE; 'could be' rearranges BAD to ABD, and 'about' wraps that round SCONDE. 'what' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have absconded is to have fled secretly, slipping away out of sight.

clue.text: One shooting bird with little resistance

parts.note: the snipe is a wading bird
R is the symbol for resistance in physics, a little one-letter form

explanation.surface: A hunter fires at a bird which puts up little fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The snipe is the bird that gave snipers their name, as hard game to shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a marksman who fires from a hidden position.

clue.text: It will fix randy journalist

parts.note: the press is the body of journalists, so press can describe a journalist
a stud is a sexually active man, a randy fellow

explanation.surface: Something that will pin down a lecherous reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'randy journalist' as a press stud: a lusty newsman. A press stud is a popper, the British term for a snap fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: A press stud is a two-part fastener that snaps together to hold clothing closed.

clue.text: Stop one believing in God around Sabbath

indicators.note: around says the word for a believer goes about the Sabbath letter

parts.note: a deist believes in a creator God from reason alone

explanation.surface: Telling a believer to cease activity around the Sabbath.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or refrain from doing something.

clue.text: One in charge of sisters, youngsters with first pair turning soft at first

indicators.note: first pair turning means the opening two letters of the word for youngsters swap places

parts.note: babes are youngsters, babies

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of the word soft

explanation.surface: A nun in charge of young novices sees the eldest pair go soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first pair turning' swaps the opening BA of BABES, giving ABBES; 'at first' takes S from 'soft'. 'soft' looks like a description of the youngsters; it only supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbess is the head of a community of nuns.

clue.text: He's first to stop intrusion

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the next word, stop

parts.note: an entry, an entering, can be an intrusion

explanation.surface: A guard is the person who gets in the way of anyone breaking in.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the guard, who is first to stop an intruder.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard on watch is the first line of defence against anyone trying to get in.

clue.text: Expedition is turning round at a great distance

indicators.note: round says the turned word is placed about the word for far away
turning says the little word is is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
afar means at a great distance

explanation.surface: A trek that loops back from far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses 'is' to SI, and 'round' splits those two letters either side of the word for far away.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an overland trip, especially to watch or hunt animals in Africa.

clue.text: Grounds for competition is a tad shaky

indicators.note: shaky suggests the letters are unsteady and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: The arenas for a contest are a bit rickety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaky' rearranges IS A TAD. 'Grounds' looks like reasons; it means sports arenas.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadia is a plural of stadium, sports arenas where contests are held.

clue.text: Aristocrat rejecting SS for RR perhaps

indicators.note: rejecting says the named letters are thrown out of the noble's title

parts.note: a marquess is a nobleman ranking above an earl
taken as written, the two letters S

explanation.surface: A nobleman swaps his Nazi-sounding initials for a luxury car badge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' drops SS from MARQUESS. RR stands for Rolls-Royce, a brand of car, so 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A marque is a make or brand of car, and Rolls-Royce is one.

clue.text: Declared it (briefly) in full

indicators.note: in says the shortened word goes inside the word for full

parts.note: sated means full, satisfied with food

indicators.note: briefly asks for the word it to be shortened by a letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone announces a thing first in short form, then at length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the I from 'it', leaving T. 'In full' looks like the opposite of briefly and a phrase of its own; 'in' is the container signal and 'full' the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stated means said or declared plainly.

clue.text: Former state in Iowa east of Gulf

indicators.note: east of in an across clue puts the following words to the right of the gulf

parts.note: a gulf is a chasm or abyss
taken as written
IA is the postal abbreviation for Iowa

explanation.surface: A one-time country located in an American state lies east of the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gulf' suggests a sea; it is a chasm. ABYSSINIA is the old name of Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia was the historical name for the empire now called Ethiopia.

clue.text: Passage about a former coin

indicators.note: about says the word for passage goes around the letter a

parts.note: a duct is a channel or passage

explanation.surface: A corridor relating to an obsolete coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning'; it puts DUCT round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A ducat was a gold or silver coin used across Europe from medieval times.

clue.text: Hanging dastard finally over violation

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first piece above the second
finally picks the last letter of the word dastard

parts.note: rape is the gravest violation of a person

explanation.surface: A villain hanged at last for a heinous crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging' suggests an execution; it is a curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: A drape is a curtain or hanging fabric.

clue.text: One of the last eight jogging trail far in quest

indicators.note: jogging shakes the letters up so they settle into a new order

explanation.surface: A runner on a long trail run in search of a place in the final rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jogging' rearranges all fifteen letters of TRAIL FAR IN QUEST; 'in' is part of the fodder, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight competitors reach the round before the semi-finals in a knockout tournament.

clue.text: Makes corrections — pieces secured by some whose job that is

indicators.note: secured by says the pieces are held inside the editors

parts.note: eds, short for editors, are the people whose job is making corrections
men are the pieces in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: Fixing errors with pieces held in place by those employed to do it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some whose job that is' points back to the definition: editors, EDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct or improve it.

clue.text: Brezhnev maybe a long time appearing in hat?

indicators.note: appearing in says the long time is placed within the word for hat

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
an eon is an immensely long time

explanation.surface: A Soviet leader seen for ages in his hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Leonid Brezhnev led the Soviet Union; 'maybe' marks him as one person with the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonid was Brezhnev's first name, so he is one example of a man called that.
